findings.finding: test_importing_dev_server_does_no_pathlib_path_arithmetic faked os.name BEFORE pathlib was first imported in the child, which defused the landmine it means to detect. On 3.11 _PosixFlavour.is_supported / _WindowsFlavour.is_supported are CLASS attributes evaluated once at pathlib import time from os.name; Path.__new__ then picks a class from the CURRENT os.name and checks that class's flag, so under a fake applied first the two agree and construction never raises. With the old derivation restored the mutation still reddened a Windows host by accident (PosixPath parses C:\... as one component so parents[1] raises IndexError) but would have passed clean on ubuntu-latest, where ci.yml runs - inert on the gate that runs most often.
Docstring asserted a mechanism the test did not exercise, and named 'PosixPath' (the Windows-host direction only) as if it were the cross-platform behaviour.

assert on bool(_SCRIPTS_DIR)/bool(_PROFILES_DIR) could not fail independently of the returncode assert above it - truthiness of a non-empty string proves only that the attributes exist, not that the derivations survived the fake.
Opening paragraph mis-stated its own census twice: 'neither name below' (there are three) and 'the three submodules that need the path on sys.path' (profile_config.py needs only _PROFILES_DIR).
Pre-existing docstring's reproduction recipe went stale: the proxy now reads _paths._SCRIPTS_DIR, so monkeypatching the package-level re-export no longer reproduces the shadowing experiment.

Claim under doubt: this is a behavior-preserving SIMPLIFY with no gate impact — DISPROVED. shared/tests/test_dev_server_windows_npm.py went 285 -> 393 lines. bloat_baseline.limit_for() gives .py files LIMIT_SOURCE=300, should_skip() does not skip shared/tests, and the file has no shipwright_bloat_baseline.json entry - a NEW crossing, 94 lines over, created by this diff. bloat_gate_on_stop.py:274 BLOCKS Stop for any session whose marker is inside the 1h TTL, and Group H raises it post-merge. Not a CI failure (bloat-check.yml makes new crossings advisory) and not a pre-commit block (anti_ratchet.py: files outside the baseline are advisory) - which is exactly why it is easy to ship past. In-tree precedent: test_dev_server_b4_surface_parity.py:8-12 exists as a separate file for precisely this situation.

Claim under doubt: test_importing_dev_server_does_no_pathlib_path_arithmetic is platform-symmetric — NOT disproved today, but its greenness rests on an unstated invariant. The child fakes os.name BEFORE importing dev_server, so every stdlib module the chain first-imports evaluates its module-scope platform branch under the fake - and the fake is 'posix' on the Windows F0 host but 'nt' on ci.yml's ubuntu-latest, so the two hosts execute different branches. Checked against CPython 3.11.15: the only module-scope os.name platform-imports reachable are shutil.py:37-40 (pre-imported, documented) and urllib/request.py:1682's nturl2path via health.py - and nturl2path is pure-Python and ships on Linux, so the ubuntu direction survives. Safe today, but one module-scope import away from ubuntu-only-red: ctypes/util.py:7 is `if os.name == "nt"`. The docstring enumerated the three modules to pre-import but never stated the rule that generated the list.
